source_text:
## Acceptance checklist (2026-09-30)

- [ ] The DOCUMENT section gives a reviewer-readable account of the implemented as-of, derivation, agreement, obligation, withdrawal, blocker-escalation, and attestation paths with their evidence.
- [ ] The DOCUMENT exit names the deferred items and their written re-arm conditions, including Joe's user-side demonstration condition for item 17.4.

---

sentences.unresolved_reason: Section heading; it frames what follows as acceptance criteria but makes no move of its own.

fragments.text: The DOCUMENT section gives a reviewer-readable account of the implemented as-of, derivation, agreement, obligation, withdrawal, blocker-escalation, and attestation paths with their evidence.
fragments.target: the DOCUMENT section of mission M-象-2000
fragments.rationale: An unchecked acceptance item: the mission is not done until the document gives a reviewer a readable account of each named path with its evidence. The move sets the standard of proof for done, not the work itself.

pattern_refs.rationale: The item defines done as an account backed by evidence for each path, not as a declaration that the paths exist; it is the mission-level form of activation-as-part-of-done.
The deliverable is reviewer-readable: the standard is an adequacy judgement by a reader (which behaviours are pinned, with what evidence), not the author's assertion of completeness.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern warns against proxies for a claimed property; here the checklist demands the direct evidence account itself, so the boundary case does not apply.
pattern_rejections.query: acceptance checklist items with observable evidence

fragments.text: names the deferred items and their written re-arm conditions
fragments.target: how the DOCUMENT exit treats deferred items
fragments.rationale: Deferral is permitted only in a hardened form: each deferred item must be named and must carry its re-arm condition in writing at the exit. This constrains the shape of an acceptable close, ruling out silent or vague deferral.

pattern_refs.rationale: The item is WR-26 applied to mission documentation: switched-off scope must carry a countable, written re-arm condition at the point of switching off, so deferral persists by decision rather than by default.
Its defer-properly branch: a deferral is legitimate only with a forward pointer the reader can chase, which is exactly what naming the items with written re-arm conditions enforces.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern exempts in-use items from scoring before judgement; this sentence is about deferring undone work with re-arm conditions, a different deferral shape.
pattern_rejections.query: defer items with written re-arm conditions

fragments.text: Joe's user-side demonstration condition for item 17.4.
fragments.target: the re-arm condition for deferred item 17.4
fragments.rationale: One deferred item is pinned to a specific, owner-assigned re-arm condition: Joe demonstrating it from the user side. The acceptance item shows the rule applied concretely, with the condition holder named.

pattern_refs.rationale: Re-arming on a user-side demonstration makes reactivation observed behaviour rather than a declaration: item 17.4 returns only when it is seen working in Joe's hands.

sentences.unresolved_reason: Markdown horizontal rule closing the checklist section; no propositional content.
